Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

immediate adjective

happening at once, without delay

also an immediate answer, immediate effect, prompt, without delay

classical

Liv. 3.1.7: fēcit statim … fastīdium cōpia
Traupman 87: immediately, statim, continuō

statim

adverb, with the verb

at once, immediately

Latin usually turns an English “immediate” into an adverb with the verb: an immediate answer is an answer given at once (statim respondēre), and Livy’s plenty “at once bred boredom”. See at once.

Other words

  • praesēns, praesentis — immediate, instant

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.122: praesēns poena, instant punishment (Lewis & Short); Cic. Clu. 34: praesentī pecūniā, with ready money (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of what is done or paid on the spot. Its first sense is present, in person, at hand (praesēns tēcum ēgī, Cic. Fam. 2.7.4), and of time, the present (see current).

  • sine morā — without delay

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 10.18.4 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • fēcit statim, ut fit, fastīdium cōpia

    plenty, as usually happens, bred immediate boredomLiv. 3.1.7

  • nīl spernat auris, nec tamen crēdat statim

    let the ear scorn nothing, and yet believe nothing at oncePhaedr. 3.10.51

See also at once, now, current, immediate.
